⚖ SHADBALA PANEL · SIX-FOLD STRENGTH
month, tz & location follow the engine inputs · strip = strength ratio sampled 4-hourly · classical 7 only (BPHS)
⚠ EXTENDED BODIES ARE NOT CLASSICAL. BPHS defines shadbala for the seven visible grahas only. Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, Rahu and Ketu have no exaltation degree, no naisargika rank, no required minimum and no slot in the vara / hora / masa / abda / tribhaga rulership cycles — those five sub-balas score zero for them, which depresses their kala. The values used here are invented: dignity from modern co-rulership (Uranus–Aquarius, Neptune–Pisces, Pluto–Aries/Scorpio), naisargika continued outward by orbital period, required minimum set to Saturn’s 300, friendships by temperament. Rahu/Ketu exaltation in Taurus/Scorpio is a genuine but disputed classical opinion (Mansagari), not BPHS. Treat every number here as a modern construction.
⚠ NAKSHATRA BALA IS NOT CLASSICAL. No shastra assigns virupa weights to the stars — Brihat Samhita treats them qualitatively (Ch.15 significations, Ch.41 Teji-Mandi). This layer is a bounded modern construction from attributes already in the engine: Vimshottari lord maitri (own star +20, mitra +15, sama 0, shatru −15; Rahu→Saturn / Ketu→Mars proxy), Muhurta-Chintamani nature (Kshipra +10 → Tikshna −12, per the market tones in the Nakshatra station), gana (deva +5 / rakshasa −5), pada navamsa-lord relation (±4, self +6), and BS 15.31 co-tenancy (Ju/Ve occupants +6, Su/Sa −6, Ma −6 or −8 retro, clamped ±10). The sum is soft-normed at ±45, scaled by transit sensitivity σ (Moon 1.0 → Saturn 0.55, outers 0.35) and the GAIN cap, then applied as a ratio multiplier. One knob gates it everywhere shadbala flows: this panel, sector panorama, the markets station, and each event’s Vishadeekaran breakdown. Nakshatra position is always sidereal regardless of the SAYANA/LAHIRI frame.
DEFAULT — the original implementation: cheshta as a speed-ratio proxy, no yuddha bala, mean sunrise, civil-day weekday, elongation-threshold paksha, hard-stepped special aspects.
